 31. Now let us examine the legality of Annexures E and G-1 to the writ petition and also the relevant provisions of law before coming to a definite finding on the points involved in the instant writ petition. In the instant writ petition three annexures namely Annexure-E which relates to the order of removal of the petitioner from service and the decision No. 1/169/2013 taken by respondent No. 5 in respect of petitioners appeal so far it relates to the recommendation of punishment of the petitioner other than removal or dismissal (Annexure-G) and Memo No. সুপবিস/৩০০-৪১/২০১৩/৮৬১ dated 6-4-2013 signed by Respondent No. 6 forwarded the decision for approval (Annexure-G-1) and decision taken and communicated through Memo No. পরিবো/তশৃপ-১৭০/৬৩০/২০১৩(১৪২০)/১২৫৪ dated 5-6-2013 by Respondent No. 4 which is communicated to the petitioner by the Respondent No. 6 vide Memo No. সুপবিস/৩০০-৩০/২০১৩/১৫৯৬ dated 27-6-2013 (Annexure-1) were challenged. The relevant provisions of law in this regard is that as far as the final show cause notice as issued by Director, Enquiry and Discipline respondent No. 4 dated 18-12-2012 has no authority to issue such letter in terms of delegation of Authority promulgated by Rural Electrification Board on 18-3-2009 only the Executive Director can issue such type of letter and, as such, the very issuance of the final show cause notice has no legal force accordingly the order of removal order dated 26-2-2013 is clear violation of delegation of power as well as provision of law and, as such, the very removal order as passed by respondent No. 4 is malafide, arbitrary and illegal. The very annexure dated 26-2-2013 has been issued in clear violation of delegation of power as well as provision of law. We also find on perusal of the relevant annexure that in the instant case the departmental proceeding was initiated against the petitioner on 15-7-2012 in terms of Article 40 of Pally Biddut Samity Service Code it should be completed within 90+30 days but in violation of provision of law it was completed on 26-2-2013 i.e. beyond the statutory period of limitation. So, the very proceeding and the decision taken against the petitioner is not at all valid and have no legal force in the eye of law. 

 37. We also find the very issuance of the final show cause notice is arbitrary, malafide, illegal and without any lawful authority. The issuance of final show cause notice as issued against the petitioner is baseless, malafide and illegal as well. We also find the decisions for reinstating the petitioner in service being the decision No. 1/169/2013 dated 23-3-2013 was duly and properly taken into consideration by the Board unanimously but the authority most illegally and arbitrarily sent the decision/ regulation to the office of the respondent No. 1 for approval is in complete violation of Article 44 of Pally Biddut Samity Service Code. We also find the very departmental proceeding initiated against the petitioner on 15-7-2012 in terms of Article 40 of Pally Biddut Samity Service Code should be completed within 90+30 days but in violation of the provisions of law it was completed on 26-2-2013 i.e. beyond the statutory period of limitation and, as such the said proceeding and decisions taken against the petitioner is not valid and have no legal force in the eye of law.
